questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Rashmi is not only smart __but very beautiful.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**but also very beautiful**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The conjunction pair is not only...but also__.
 
• Correlative conjunctions always come in pairs and they relate one part of the sentence to the other. "Not only... but also" can be used to connect either nouns or clauses. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Using *not only . . . but also***** in a sentence**, **parallelism**** should be the goal**. It means that the words following both parts of this correlative conjunction (i.e., *not only* and *but also*) should belong to the same parts of speech. For example, if a verb follows *not only*, then a verb should also follow *but also*. Using different parts of speech after each part of *not only . . . but also* makes the sentence imbalanced and, frankly, just awkward. 

 **Example: **He’s not only intelligent but also has a great sense of humor.

 He’s not only intelligent but also funny.

 

**Thus the correct sentence will be:** *Rashmi is not only smart but also very beautiful.*

Sunil __have been working__ as a personal assistant to the Director for two years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'has been working.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the plural form of the verb ''have'' is incorrect.
 
• The subject 'Sunil' in the given sentence is a singular subject.
 
• The singular form of the verb 'has' should be used with the singular subject 'Sunil'.
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the verb ''has'' should be used in place of the plural form 'have'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *Sunil **has been working** as a personal assistant to the Director for two years*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural). (विषय और क्रिया एक दूसरे के साथ संख्या (एकवचन या बहुवचन) में सहमत होना चाहिए)
 
• Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if the subject is plural, its verb must also be plural. (इस प्रकार, यदि कोई विषय एकवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी एकवचन होनी चाहिए ; यदि विषय बहुवचन है , तो उसकी क्रिया भी बहुवचन होनी चाहिए)

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

__
 
• रेखांकित खंड में क्रिया 'have' का बहुवचन रूप गलत है ।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में subject 'Sunil' एक एकवचन subject है।
 
• क्रिया का एकवचन रूप 'has', एकवचन subject 'Sunil' के साथ प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• इसलिए बहुवचन क्रिया 'have' के स्थान पर एकवचन क्रिया 'has' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

सही वाक्य: *Sunil has been working as a personal assistant to the Director for two years*.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the underlined part of the following sentence.**

It has been raining **__from__** morning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"since."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"since"** is used to indicate the starting point of a period of time.
 
• It refers to a time (an action that begun in the past and is still continuing).
 
• In this sentence, **"since" **is the most appropriate option as it indicates that the rain started in the morning and is still continuing.
 
 
• **Example**: *We have been married **since**__ 1996.*
 
 
 
• The word **"from"** is used to refer to a place or time at which any event/action/journey starts/initiates. The word since is used to refer to the time passed between then and now.
 __
 
• **Example**: *The movie will run **from**__ 10:00 a.m to 12:00 p.m.*
 
 
 
• The word **"for"** would indicate a duration of time, but it doesn't fit the context of the sentence as it doesn't convey that the rain is still ongoing.
 __
 
• **Example**: *I was waiting **for**__ an hour.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 

**Correct sentence**: *It has been raining __**since**__ morning.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: "For"** indicates a duration of time.

 
 
• **Example**: *"I have been waiting **for**__ two hours."*
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "Though" **indicates a contrast or concession.
 __
 
• **Example**: *"**Though**__ it was raining, we still went for a walk."*
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "Till"** indicates an end point.
 __
 
• **Example**: *"The store is open **till**__ 10 PM."*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

You are the __beautiful__ woman I have ever seen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **most beautiful.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the correct superlative form of the adjective should be used.
 
• The term **'beautiful'** is an **adjective** that can be modified to its **superlative **form for comparison.
 
• The presence of **'the' **before 'beautiful' hints at the fact that the** superlative form **of **'beautiful' **should be used.
 
• The correct superlative form of **'beautiful'** is **'most beautiful'**, indicating that no other woman is more beautiful than the one being referred to.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *You are the most beautiful woman I have ever seen*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In English grammar, adjectives have three degrees of comparison: positive, comparative, and superlative.
 
 
• **Positive degree:** describes a single item/person (e.g., beautiful).
 
• **Comparative degree:** compares two items/people (e.g., more beautiful).
 
• **Superlative degree:** compares more than two items/people (e.g., most beautiful).

She __finished her quickly breakfast__ and rushed to school.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **syntax: subject + verb + object + adverb.**

• Always remember this rule when using such adjectives in comparative degrees.
</ul

questions.solution:

• The subject of the sentence is "**My friend Meera and her mother**", which is **plural**.
 
• Therefore, **the verb must also be plural to agree with the subject**.
 
• "**Are visiting**" is the correct verb form for a plural subject.
 
• Using "**is visiting**" with a plural subject is grammatically incorrect.

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

**Corrected sentence**: *My friend Meera and her mother are visiting me this weekend.*
